title: Odds and Probability
objective: After this level you can turn odds like "3 to 1 against" into a probability and back again.
summary: Odds compare the chances against with the chances for; probability compares the chances for with the whole. Add the two numbers of the odds to find the whole: 3 to 1 against is 1 in 4.

cards.headline: Pick a card. The odds it's a heart are "3 to 1 against". What's the chance?
cards.body: Not 3 in 4, and not 1 in 3. Odds and probability are two ways of saying the same chance, and they're easy to mix up. By the end of this level you'll switch between them in your head.

cards.headline: Odds compare two piles. Probability uses the whole deck.
cards.body: A standard deck has 52 cards in four suits of 13. Draw one: 13 cards are hearts and 39 aren't. Odds compare the chances against with the chances for: 39 to 13, which shrinks to 3 to 1 against. Probability compares the hearts with the whole deck: 13 out of 52, or 1 in 4. Same draw, same chance, two different ways of saying it.

cards.headline: Odds to probability: add the two numbers
cards.body: To turn odds into a chance, add both numbers to find the whole. "3 to 1 against" means 3 ways to lose and 1 way to win, 4 in all. So the chance of winning is 1 in 4, or 25%. It's Chapter 1's question again: out of what? For odds, the whole is hiding in plain sight. You just have to add it up.

cards.fact: Going back, split the whole into wins and losses.
cards.context: A 1 in 5 chance means 1 win to 4 losses: 4 to 1 against. Likely events flip around. An 80% chance is 80 wins to 20 losses, which shrinks to 4 to 1 in favor. And a 50% chance is 1 to 1, a true toss-up.

mascot.line: People mix these up all the time. "To" compares wins with losses. "In" compares wins with everything.

cards.headline: Odds and chances: switched
learned: Probability compares for with the whole
Odds to chance: add the two numbers

questions.prompt: The odds of drawing a heart from a full deck are 3 to 1 against. What is the chance of drawing one?

options.label: 1 in 3
options.rationale: That divides 1 by 3; the whole is 3 plus 1, which is 4.

options.label: 3 in 4
options.rationale: That's the chance of not drawing a heart.

options.label: 3 in 1
options.rationale: A chance can't be more than the whole.

questions.explanation: 3 to 1 against means 3 losing cards for every winning one: 4 in all, so the chance is 1 in 4 (13 hearts out of 52).

questions.prompt: How do you turn odds of 4 to 1 against into a probability?

options.label: Add 4 and 1 to find the whole: a 1 in 5 chance
Divide 1 by 4: a 1 in 4 chance
options.rationale: Odds compare wins with losses, so the whole is 4 plus 1.

options.label: Subtract 1 from 4: a 3 in 4 chance
options.rationale: Subtracting mixes up the two piles; add them instead.

options.label: Read it as 4%
options.rationale: Odds are not a percent; add the two numbers to get the whole.

questions.explanation: Odds of 4 to 1 against mean 4 ways to lose and 1 to win. Adding gives the whole, 5, so the chance is 1 in 5.

questions.prompt: Odds of 9 to 1 against make a 1 in 10 chance. Using Level 7's "1 in N" switch, what percent is that?

options.rationale: That uses the 9 from the odds; the chance is 1 in 10.

questions.explanation: Add 9 and 1 to get the whole, 10. Then 100 ÷ 10 turns "1 in 10" into 10%.
